Two other interesting facts emerged from the tests descrined in
Section 4.1.5. Firstly, because a nead build up in the drains due to
closure of the taps was maintained without leakage from around the outside
of the drain, the indications are that the adjacent soii nad collapsed
onto the drain liner. Also, because there was no increase in water level
in the perched water table, it can be assumed that no transfer of water
between aquifers occurred. One conclusion made is that, in tnis
particular case, it was unnecessary to form a grouted impermeaple invert
or annulus because the surrounding soil had sealed the annulus by
collapsing onto the drain liner. In this situation, the provision of a
drain liner with an impermeable invert is all that is required.

Tne second point wortny of note concerns the filtering action of the

Upon reopening, a significant loss of fines occurred during the first 24
hours, during which time a new filter formed around the screen and the
discharge suosequently cleared. Obviously a filter that had initially
been satisfactory, failed under the large pressure differential that
existed on drain reopening. It may oe possiple to use tne technique of

4.3 EFFECTS OF GROUNDWATER CHEMISTRY ON DRAIN PERFORMANCE

Groundwater samples were taken fran the trial norizontal drains in
January 1984 and sent to the Public Works Laboratories for analysis. The
analysis report stated that the water samples contained very low con-
centrations of substances which may be precipitated from solution, but
tnere was very little danger of the drainage slots being clogged provided
that the water quality is maintained.
